font.family: Computer Modern (LaTeX serif, CMU Serif) for all text and math; no sans-serif body text
font.weight: regular (400); emphasis comes from colour, not bold

motion.signature: Shapes are drawn on and morph into one another instead of cutting. Concentric rings unroll into a triangle, a cube splits into slabs, and a pi creature reacts with blinks and eye movements. Colour gradients from cyan to green carry the meaning, and key terms are tinted in the quote or caption.

layout: Pure black canvas with generous empty space. The visual sits off-centre or top-left, with braces and labels (3, R, dx) attached to it and the formula or caption placed beside or beneath. Titles are centred at the top in light cyan. A thin white rectangle frames the 3D geometry scenes, and a row of rounded cyan chapter icons sits above the 'Essence of calculus' headings.
format_reason: The content is geometric and algebraic and teaches by continuous transformation of shapes and equations, which programmatic animation (Manim-style) does well. A whiteboard or avatar would lose that.
